decisions.reason: As the publicly presented flagship of the firm's sustainable reusable-packaging direction, the citrus crate carries heavy visible commitment, and any weak uptake can still be attributed to seasonal and pandemic-related adoption delays.
The multi-model foldable large container line has its own page and substantial tooling investment, and it is central to returnable logistics, so persistence is justified.
Stackable crates are core portfolio items with sunk mold costs across several models, and withdrawing them would contradict earlier commitments despite their low website visibility.
Rackable pallets are a core offering with multi-model tooling already paid for, and disappointing results can be blamed on temporary supply-chain disruption.
This single pallet variant has its own page and sunk mold costs, so management would keep it and attribute weak sales to temporary market conditions, though it is the most expendable item.
